gaps.criterion_why: A player watching a grass fire would see whether it runs downwind rather than just being blocked sideways, so asking the scene to tell wind-following apart from a wind-blind lane block, with a reversed-wind case and a clean start, is a fair bar that a correct mod can pass.
gaps.judge_criterion_why: His bar is that the fire walks with the wind. A scene that never varies the wind cannot show the wind is the cause, and the contract requires a control that rules out the plausible alternative.
gaps.observed: The leaf asks that the player 'sees it run with the wind, away from where it lit, and not spread evenly to every side', and that it 'must not read as a fire that spreads the same way whatever the wind'. Its red is 'a line burns as far upwind as downwind'. The scene's action lights 'a short line at the upwind end of each strip', so the strip holds no upwind grass to read. Its only varied input is the setting: one wind, 'the wind set across them' (the script calls SetWindForTest "90" once, east). The script lights the line at x+2.
